assignedRole.bio: You are the investigator clutching a battered notebook and a piercing glare. You observe everyone's body language and piece together hidden clues.
assignedRole.secretObjective: Unmask the killer before dessert cocktails! During cocktail hour, pull two people aside and whisper: 'I know what you did in Vienna.' Gauge their reaction.

clueCards.label: Your Alibi (Where you were)
clueCards.text: At 8:45 PM, you were in the Foyer questioning the Butler about who arrived without an invitation.

clueCards.label: Witness Intel (What you saw)
clueCards.text: You noticed a pair of dark evening gloves resting on the study side table that vanished right before 9:00 PM.

clueCards.label: Cleared Evidence (Rule this out!)
clueCards.text: You inspected the fireplace poker in the Parlour—it is coated in thick undisturbed soot and was NOT used.

assignedRole.costumeGuide: Trench coat, tweed blazer, vintage fedora, pocket notepad, magnifying glass or spectacles.
assignedRole.doorPasscode: WHISPER AT DOOR: 'The game is afoot.'

assignedRole.bio: You are the glamorous guest with an iron will and a deadly secret. You smile warmly at everyone, sip your cocktail, and deflect all suspicion.
assignedRole.secretObjective: You did it—or you are orchestrating it tonight! Your goal is to deflect suspicion onto the Doctor or the Butler. Claim you were getting a savoury when the lights went out.

clueCards.label: The Murder Weapon
clueCards.text: The Antique Silver Letter Opener (swiped from the study desk right after luring Birdie away with the stolen treats).

clueCards.label: The Motive / The Reason
clueCards.text: Furious resentment that the Woman of the Manor chose her prized companion Birdie over her own family, telling you that you don't truly belong in this household!

clueCards.label: Your Accomplice
clueCards.text: The Accomplice (The Loyal Shadow) swiped Birdie's treats to lure the companion away and will vouch for your false alibi.

assignedRole.costumeGuide: Dramatic black or crimson attire, velvet or lace, gloves, confident smile.
assignedRole.doorPasscode: WHISPER AT DOOR: 'A spider spins at midnight.'

assignedRole.bio: The physician who knows dark medical secrets. You carry an eye for detail, rare botanicals, and unusual antidotes.
assignedRole.secretObjective: Protect innocence. You carry an antidote. When the murder occurs, loudly examine the body/scene and cast doubt on exotic poisons.

clueCards.label: Your Alibi (Where you were)
clueCards.text: At 8:45 PM, you were in the dining area pouring a drink and admiring the antique silver decanter.

clueCards.label: Witness Intel (What you saw)
clueCards.text: You examined Birdie's empty dish in passing—there was no poison, only evidence that the treats had been hastily scooped out.

clueCards.label: Cleared Evidence (Rule this out!)
clueCards.text: You tested the punch bowl with silver litmus—it is completely free of poison. The strike was physical.

assignedRole.costumeGuide: Velvet dinner jacket or formal vest, vintage pocket watch, antique vial or leather notebook.
assignedRole.doorPasscode: WHISPER AT DOOR: 'First, do no harm.'

assignedRole.bio: The loyal confidant who manages correspondence, secret debts, and private alliances. You protect your partner at all costs.
assignedRole.secretObjective: Protect The Murderer at all costs. Plant a false clue or drop a hint that implicates someone else during cocktails.

clueCards.label: Your Mastermind
clueCards.text: The Murderer is your secret partner. You swiped Birdie's treats to lure the companion away from the study.

clueCards.label: Your Fabricated Alibi
clueCards.text: Swear to everyone that you and the Murderer were in the Parlour discussing art when the argument through closed doors occurred.

clueCards.label: Your Diversion Task
clueCards.text: Steer suspicion toward the Butler by whispering that he was furious about having to serve Birdie silver platters.

assignedRole.costumeGuide: Sharp formal suit or elegant evening wear, pocket square, charming and discreet presence.
assignedRole.doorPasscode: WHISPER AT DOOR: 'The ink never dries.'
